title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 2 Sep 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.86 km2 to 29.75 km2, or -6.6%. Over these 60 days HH rose across the land while HV barely moved.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 2.11 km2. Mean HV moved by -0.06 dB and mean HH rose by 0.5 dB. In HH, 2.05 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.24 km2 darker; in HV, 0.49 km2 turned brighter and 0.38 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 0.87 km2 brighter in HH and rose 0.57 dB. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes rose 0.48 dB in HH. Built-up land, which should not change, rose 0.62 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's level record would confirm it. Possible cause for higher HH on all types, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the two acquisitions; stable targets on more dates would check it. Possible cause on the fields: drier, rougher soil after harvest.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 12.7% and 8.6% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Report the 2.11 km2 loss alongside the dam's own figures for the 60 days. Keep HH changes of under one dB out of any decision until calibration is checked.
